methods: Independent source and schema examination of authentication, pilot, privacy, support, Job Loop next actions and administration metrics.
Historical local outreach assets reviewed only as unsent assets; no peer or prior audit grades read.
Official Supabase SMTP and Gmail sender guidance read 2026-10-14.
Four recommendation-only email drafts checked with email-sequence analyzer: 75/100 heuristic copy score; no delivery or effectiveness claim.
not_tested: SMTP configuration, DNS authentication, received emails or inbox placement
Any private mailbox, actual subscriber data, provider dashboard or deliverability logs
No emails, drafts into accounts, subscriptions, paid calls or runtime mutations

criteria.name: Permission boundaries and truthful expectations
criteria.evidence: PilotLanding110–129, ProductPage162–166 and JobLoopPanels74 clearly bound contact and processing.

criteria.name: Consent, preferences and suppression readiness
criteria.evidence: Auth149–169 has no lifecycle choice; bounded source/schema search found no lifecycle unsubscribe or suppression contract.

criteria.name: Task relevance and activation design
criteria.evidence: JobLoopPanels27–33 provides actionable states; lifecycle email implementation and candidate response are untested.

criteria.name: Transactional sender readiness
criteria.evidence: AuthContext100–118 uses supported SDK; AUTH-REPAIR31 leaves live delivery checks pending; no SMTP/DNS evidence inspected.

criteria.name: Repeat usefulness and measurement
criteria.evidence: Due dates and candidate actions exist; admin snapshot65,85–86 correctly limits metrics but has no email attribution.

strengths: No forced email capture for first value.
Pilot request explicitly remains unsent; support records do not claim email delivery.
Preparation consent, inbox connection and draft creation are separate and no employer send action is provided.
Next-step resolver, candidate due dates and candid metric definitions are a practical basis for a small lifecycle pilot.

findings.problem: A future lifecycle send has no source-visible purpose-specific permission, unsubscribe or suppression contract; signup, pilot contact and preparation consent must not become mailing-list permission.

evidence.detail: Signup captures account credentials; inspected form has no lifecycle email choice.
Recurring consent authorizes rules-based preparation, not candidate email delivery.
Pilot request remains in memory and is sent only by the candidate's chosen email app.
Inspected privacy content describes service processing but no email subscription lifecycle; bounded src/schema search found no newsletter suppression or unsubscribe implementation.

findings.recommendation: Before any optional lifecycle mail, add separate unchecked choices for onboarding help, dated-action reminders and occasional tips. Record purpose, address verification, timestamp, source and wording version. Keep operational auth separate. Implement signed unsubscribe without login, global optional-mail suppression, hard-bounce/complaint suppression and send-time rechecks. Never import historical coach prospects into this program.
acceptance_criteria: Unconsented signup, draft request, Google sign-in and recurring preparation never enqueue optional mail.
Opt-out, complaint, hard bounce, erasure and duplicate webhook fixtures suppress queued optional sends; opt-out survives later sign-in.
Unsubscribe works without login; essential user-requested auth remains separately classified.
findings.cost_effect: No expenditure now; small storage/engineering cost later; prevent unnecessary mail and a paid marketing platform during the ten-user pilot.

findings.problem: Source-supported auth requests are not evidence of actual external confirmation/recovery delivery or sender authentication. Operational readiness remains unverified.

evidence.detail: Signup calls supported Supabase SDK; password recovery at line118 requests /auth/reset.
Document explicitly leaves live delivery and allowlisting as release checks.
No SMTP settings, DNS verification, received headers or delivery logs inspected; no delivery test performed.
Official documentation read 2026-10-14: default SMTP is restricted, best effort, currently two messages/hour; advises separate auth/marketing streams and authentication.

findings.recommendation: Create an owner-run release checklist for authorized synthetic accounts: confirmation policy, recovery, expiry, resend throttles, redirects and provider events. Keep auth template, sender and reputation distinct from lifecycle promotions. Verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC and actual received headers before promising delivery; do not activate SMTP in this audit.
acceptance_criteria: Document the configured confirmation policy and observed recovery outcome, including missing-message recovery guidance.
Authorized tests cover expired links, wrong browser, throttling, duplicate clicks and correct production redirect.
Evidence includes provider acceptance versus inbox receipt separately; no promotional CTA in auth templates.
dependencies: Owner access to existing sender/DNS configuration
findings.cost_effect: Audit costs $0; future SMTP cost not priced or approved and is outside the $50 AI/search ceiling.

findings.problem: The product has useful next-step states but no source-visible email lifecycle that turns those states into timely, permissioned help. This is deferred readiness, not a broken existing delivery promise.

evidence.detail: Next-action selection distinguishes missing profile, unconfirmed facts, reviewable documents, first vacancy and repeat application.
First check works without signup; creating an account is optional for private saving.

findings.recommendation: Test the four recommendation-only drafts below with consenting pilot participants. Reuse the existing next-action resolver and suppress on task completion. Avoid collecting guest email merely to trigger abandonment mail.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture journeys choose exactly one relevant task and CTA; completion cancels queued help.
Student examples preserve academic contributions; MBA/professional examples preserve truthful source facts.
Guest first check remains usable without email or account.
findings.cost_effect: Static copy and existing state reuse; no paid model generation or ESP purchase needed for draft testing.

findings.problem: Existing due dates and preparation schedules are distinct; converting every scheduled run into mail would create noise and could reveal a discreet job search.

evidence.detail: Due/upcoming actions use candidate-selected dates and exclude offer/rejected/withdrawn.
Daily/weekdays/weekly scheduler consent is for preparation and has pause/cancel controls.

findings.recommendation: Require a separate reminder choice, personal address confirmation, local send window and discreet-subject option. Aggregate one daily digest only when actionable; cap optional lifecycle mail to two/week initially. Recheck latest state at dispatch. Stop on search pause/end, revoked facts, erased data or withdrawn/closed tasks. Never auto-contact employers.
acceptance_criteria: Timezone-boundary, duplicate-dispatch, completed-before-send and pause-before-send fixtures produce at most one appropriate notification.
No employer names, role details, CV attachments, private receipt tokens or source quotations appear in subjects or URLs.
A successful job-search exit stops reminders and is not counted as failed retention.
findings.cost_effect: Bounded message volume; $0 current activation; future mail charges separate from AI/search budget.

findings.problem: Current product metrics provide activation evidence but cannot attribute optional email usefulness; automated completed runs must not be counted as candidate return.

evidence.detail: Download-request metric explicitly does not establish browser download completion.
Week-two candidate return is distinct from repeat completed preparation, which includes schedules.

findings.recommendation: Log minimal purpose/template/task identifiers and eligible, suppressed, queued, provider-accepted, bounced, complained and unsubscribed outcomes. Associate a clicked message with the next meaningful candidate action in a declared seven-day window, without CV/employer data in tracking. Report counts and denominators; do not optimize opens or conduct A/B significance tests on ten people.
acceptance_criteria: Report first approved document and voluntary second-vacancy preparation separately from automated runs.
One task completed after multiple clicks counts once; delivery acceptance is not an inbox or action claim.
Record complaints/opt-outs and contextual feedback alongside activation; no benchmark/conversion promises.
findings.cost_effect: Reuse existing database; no paid analytics suite or tracking pixel required.

open_questions: Which existing sender, domain authentication and operational templates are configured? No secrets are needed in the report.
Do pilot participants want email, and which reminder purposes are worth receiving? Validate before implementation.
What sender identity, contact address, retention and recipient-jurisdiction requirements will the owner approve before optional sends?
do_not_build_now: No historical coach-prospect import, cold nurture, automatic contact or employer follow-ups.
No generic newsletter, daily scheduled-run announcements, upgrade/trial-expiry sequence, paid ESP purchase or new subscription.
No CV attachments or employer details in notifications; no open-rate target or claimed email conversion uplift.
No separate persona campaign stacks; reuse task states and short truthful examples.
